items.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995
items.q: The interviewee only responds to the interviewer's narrative about Neal Hefti and Count Basie; no personal interaction or relationship between Jillean Williams and Neal Hefti is described.

ctx.x: He always will be. Because he was the key. Clark Terry this morning, it’s often been written that the real secret to Bill Basie was that he always knew the right tempo for a tune. And Clark told a story of “L’il Darling?”
Yeah, when Neal Hefti brought it in.

When Neal Hefti brought it in and said, “here’s the tempo.” And Basie says, “no, this is the tempo.” And they played it that way and it was a huge hit. And as Clark says, if they’d played it with Hefti’s speed, it would have been another “who heard of it?”
